title: Oxide raises $445M on profitability and AI demand
key_facts: Oxide Computer raised $445 million in a Series D round.
Eclipse Capital led, joined by AMD Ventures, Riot Ventures, Jane Street, Atreides Management and USIT.
Oxide sells a pre-integrated data center rack combining computing, storage and networking, built on AMD processors.
CEO Steve Tuck says Oxide has had to scale manufacturing capacity 20 times over the past 12 months and demand still exceeds supply.
The funds will go to materials and manufacturing scale.
USIT led Oxide's previous $200 million raise in February.
In August Oxide disclosed plans for a sled that can host a graphics card.
quote_evidence: Data center hardware startup Oxide Computer Inc. today announced that it has raised $445 million in funding.

“The accelerating pace of on-prem cloud computing projects has required us to scale manufacturing capacity by 20x over the past 12 months, and yet demand still exceeds supply,” said Oxide co-founder and Chief Executive Steve Tuck.
why_it_matters_hint: Demand for on-site cloud hardware is outrunning supply, per the CEO.
notes: The investing.com headline mentions profitability, which the SiliconANGLE article does not; profitability is not claimed here. Round also covered by PR Newswire, citybiz, Unite.AI and Wowtale (headlines seen).
